review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the one @[simp] lemma (line 385), the public definition prodDirectSumMap, and how downstream files use these. I also checked the Mathlib simp lemmas ExteriorAlgebra.map_apply_ιMulti, exteriorPower.ιMulti_apply_coe and exteriorPower.coe_map. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour. Most of the file is private scaffolding, where simp attributes are not relevant. I found no rewrite cycle. The only gap I found is the missing simp API for prodDirectSumMap. The two coe_prodEquivDirectSum_symm_of_tmul lemmas overlap, but I left that out because it is a weaker point.

findings.excerpt: noncomputable def prodDirectSumMap (k : ℕ) (f : P →ₗ[R] P') (g : Q →ₗ[R] Q') :
findings.problem: prodDirectSumMap is a public definition built from DirectSum.lmap and TensorProduct.map, and it has no simp or evaluation lemma. Its public-facing partner, the inverse of prodEquivDirectSum, does get a @[simp] evaluation lemma on `DirectSum.of … i (a ⊗ₜ b)`. A user whose goal contains `prodDirectSumMap R P Q k f g (DirectSum.of _ i (a ⊗ₜ b))` has no lemma to reduce it to `DirectSum.of _ i (exteriorPower.map i.1 f a ⊗ₜ exteriorPower.map (k - i.1) g b)`. The file's own naturality proof has to unfold the definition by hand with `rw [prodDirectSumMap, DirectSum.lmap_of, TensorProduct.map_tmul]`, which exposes the implementation.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma right after the definition, tagged @[simp]: `prodDirectSumMap R P Q k f g (DirectSum.of (fun j : Fin (k+1) ↦ (⋀[R]^j.1 P) ⊗[R] (⋀[R]^(k - j.1) Q)) i (a ⊗ₜ[R] b)) = DirectSum.of (fun j : Fin (k+1) ↦ (⋀[R]^j.1 P') ⊗[R] (⋀[R]^(k - j.1) Q')) i (exteriorPower.map i.1 f a ⊗ₜ[R] exteriorPower.map (k - i.1) g b)`. Prove it by `simp [prodDirectSumMap]` or with the existing three-step rewrite. Then use it in `prodEquivDirectSum_symm_naturality` in place of the manual unfolding. The right-hand side is a different shape built from `exteriorPower.map`, so the rule cannot loop.
findings.benefit: Users and later proofs can reduce `prodDirectSumMap` on pure tensors with `simp`, and together with the existing @[simp] lemma `coe_prodEquivDirectSum_symm_of_tmul` this gives a usable simp set for naturality computations. The naturality proof no longer needs to unfold the definition.
